newsitem.title: UK: Analysts impressed by Clyde's defence.
newsitem.headline: Analysts impressed by Clyde's defence.

text.p: Clyde Petroleum Plc on Tuesday added extra fuel to analysts' conviction that the company deserves a higher bid than the 105 pence per share offered by Gulf Canada Resoruces.
The Canadian firm still has to react to Clyde's latest defence document, which said the UK firm's net assets were independently valued at at least 120 pence per share.
"The asset value solidly underpins that 105 is way too low," said a leading analyst, who declined to be named.

Gulf Canada will have to raise its offer substantially to probably over 130 pence to try to convince Clyde's major shareholders to hand over their shares, said Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
But drastically increasing the bid might make it look unconvinving after Gulf Canada's rubbishing of Clyde's previous defence arguments, Lunshof added.
"Anything in the way of a big increase would make Gulf Canada look odd," said Lunshof.
It was the first time Clyde pointed at its net asset value to try to show that Gulf Canada's offer was too low, having underlined its point earlier by using the cash flow multiple method.
The Canadian firm, which had called its offer "full and generous", has dismissed the cash flow argument, adding net asset value was the approriate method.
Shares in Clyde eased 1-1/2 pence to 117, indicating that investors were biding their time, waiting for Gulf Canada to announce its next move.
"There wasn't perhaps enough in it (the Clyde defence) to make people really excited about the prospects of somebody coming in bidding a lot more," an analyst said.
"The feeling is that for the moment it is probably safer to bet that the only game in town is Gulf Canada," he added.
